2026 Yukon River Salmon Fall Fishery Announcement #13 Coastal District, District 1, and District 2 Subsistence Fishing Schedule Emergency Order Number 3-S-FY-06-26

Districts Affected: Lower Yukon Area

As of August 25, the Yukon River fall chum salmon run is projecting to be above the upper end of the drainagewide escapement goal of 300,000–600,000 fish. With the fall chum salmon run projecting to meet both its drainagewide escapement goal and Alaska tributary escapement goals, subsistence fishing restrictions can be relaxed in tributaries where Canadian-origin fall chum salmon stocks will not be intercepted. Canadian treaty goals are not anticipated to be met even with a run size above the upper end of the drainagewide escapement goal range, based on previous season’s performance of those stocks and genetic data of the 2026 run to date. Therefore, the Yukon River mainstem must remain closed to protect Canadian-origin fall chum salmon as they make their way upriver.

The coho salmon run is past its historic midpoint, and current passage estimates are well below average. Subsistence fishing for coho salmon will remain closed but we will continue to monitor passage to identify any potential fishing opportunities.

Subsistence Management Actions:

Coastal District, District 1, and District 2 (from the Naskonat Peninsula, north to Point Romanof, and upstream to the tip of Cone Point, which includes the Black River and the communities of Chevak, Hooper Bay, Scammon Bay, Emmonak, Nunam Iqua, Alakanuk, Kotlik, Mountain Village, Pitkas Point, St. Mary’s, Pilot Station, and Marshall):

Subsistence fishing for Chinook, chum, and coho salmon is closed and these salmon species must be released alive. Gillnets of 4-inch or smaller mesh may be used to target nonsalmon from noon Thursdays, through noon Sundays. Nets are restricted to 60-feet or less in length and must be operated as a set net near shore. Fishing for nonsalmon remains open 24 hours a day, seven days per week with nonlethal or selective gear types including manned fish wheels, hook and line with a rod or pole, dip net, beach seine, hand line, longline, and fyke net. Pink and sockeye salmon may be retained.

In all tributaries of the Yukon River, except the Black River:

Effective 1:00 p.m. Wednesday, August 26, subsistence fishing for chum salmon and nonsalmon, 500 feet upstream from the mainstem or 1 mile inland from the coast, will open 24 hours per day, 7 days per week with selective gear types including manned fish wheels, hook and line with a rod or pole, dip net, beach seine, hand line, longline, and fyke net. Subsistence

Coastal District, District 1, and District 2 Subsistence Fishing Schedule

August 26, 2026

fishing in the Yukon River mainstem and the Black River for Chinook, chum, and coho salmon remains closed.

6-inch or Smaller Mesh Gillnet Nonsalmon Opportunity in Designated Areas

Subsistence fishing for whitefish and other nonsalmon species with 6-inch or smaller mesh set gillnets remains open only in designated nonsalmon areas until further notice. Set gillnets are restricted 60feet or shorter in length and cannot block more than ½ width of any waterway. Please see Fall Season Advisory Announcements #1 and #2 for the named lists, GPS coordinates, and maps of these designated areas. Links to Advisory Announcements and maps are shared on the ADFG – Yukon River Fishing Facebook page.

Federal Special Action

The Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) have coordinated on this advisory announcement. The USFWS Federal Inseason Manager has issued a separate Federal special action TSA 03-FC-08-26 with the same fishing schedule and restrictions in waters adjacent to Federal Land. However, in federal public waters of these drainages, chum salmon harvest is limited to federally qualified subsistence users of the Yukon River drainage. For additional information concerning Yukon River Federal Special Actions contact the USFWS Federal Yukon River Subsistence Fishery Manager, Holly Carroll; holly_carroll@fws.gov, (907) 351-3029 or Assistant Manager, Keith Herron; keith_herron@fws.gov, (907) 3345391.

This is an announcement by the ADF&G in cooperation with the USFWS. Federal Special Actions will be posted on www.doi.gov/subsistence/fisheries-special-actions and shared on Facebook at www.facebook.com/subsistencealaska. To receive advisory announcements by email, sign up at www.cfnews.adfg.alaska.gov.
